tob-10479: In 1537 Martin Luther drafted these articles as a bold statement of what Protestants believed, written for a church council that never happened. They sharpen the break with Rome on the pope, the Mass, and salvation by faith alone. Adopted into the Lutheran confessions, they remain a key to understanding why the Reformation could not be reconciled with Catholicism.
tob-4179: Hafiz of Shiraz is Persia’s best-loved poet — his wine-songs of longing are on every Persian tongue. Gertrude Bell, the famed traveler, turned a choice of them into English verse of rare grace. Her versions let the West taste the honey of the Persian original.
cia-0000118679: A March 1964 report on the infiltration of 2,000 Viet Cong fighters from North Vietnam into the South. Hanoi was steadily feeding men down the Ho Chi Minh Trail, and American analysts counted them like an approaching storm. The document is the war's math — numbers that would soon demand American troops.
cia-0000119579: A special report estimated to date from January 1966 on Czechoslovakia beginning a new economic program — the archive's spelling says beings. Prague was trying market-style reforms to save a failing planned economy. The document captures the economic experiment that would help spark the Prague Spring two years later.
cia-0000126879: A July 1968 study of the Soviet decision to intervene — written weeks before the tanks rolled. Analysts were trying to read the Kremlin's mind: would Moscow dare? The document is prediction at the edge of the event — the invasion, foreseen but not stopped.
cia-0000126979: A July 1975 National Intelligence Bulletin on China and Angola — Beijing's play in the coming civil war. China backed the FNLA faction, adding a third superpower to the proxy fight. The document shows the Angola crisis as a three-cornered contest, not just a Cold War duel.
cia-0000132279: Situation Report 588: Iraqis seeking asylum in Turkey, and the Arab Maghreb — the truncated title hints at North Africa's stance. Refugees were fleeing; Arab states were choosing sides. The document captures the human tide and the diplomatic arithmetic together.
cia-0000132479: Item 10 in the April 1960 series: a new guerrilla incursion in Nicaragua. The Somoza dictatorship faced its challengers. The document is the incursion, reported: the rebels, crossing.
cia-0000132579: A 1960 report: Peru possibly breaking diplomatic relations with Cuba. Lima was moving toward the divorce. The document is the maybe: the break, pending.
cia-0000136179: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on Calligeris and company, the recovery of arms and organizers — the truncated title suggests more. The aftermath accounting. The document is the recovery: the arms, reclaimed.
cia-0000136979: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN on scheduling inspection teams. The checkers, scheduled. The document is the timetable: the teams, deployed.
cia-0000138979: A 1946 military information report on Russian army strength. The numbers, counted. The document is the strength: the army, measured.
cia-0000141179: An estimated 1961 official superior's report of injury and death — for Crisp-someone, the truncated title cuts off. The casualty, recorded. The entry is the report: the loss, formalized.
un-ga-res-a-69-79: Resolution A/69/79, cataloged with the year 2009 — the mismatch again. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.

un-sc-res-179: Security Council Resolution 179, adopted in 1963. The early-sixties Council at work. The number and year are preserved; the decision belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-379: Security Council Resolution 379, adopted in 1975. The Council deciding. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-979: Security Council Resolution 979, adopted in 1995 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-2679: Security Council Resolution 2679, adopted in 2022 — aligned. The deliberations rolled on. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
cia-0000132679: A 1961 CIA file titled Cuba, numbered 0000132679. The bare title again — the archive's shorthand for a full folder. The entry is the shorthand: the island, filed.
cia-0000132779: A 1960 CIA Cuban developments file — number 0000132779. The series neared its run's end. The entry is the near-end: the series, closing.
cia-0000135679: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135679. The invasion force's own words, archived. The document is the archive: the words, kept.
cia-0000136779: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136779. The exiles' Spanish record, another installment. The entry is the installment: the record, continued.
cia-0000139479: A 1988 CIA file on Project Sun Streak — number 0000139479. The psychic program, preserved. The document is the preservation: the project, filed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d79: A memorandum by the commanding general of the Army Service Forces, Somervell — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 79. The logistics chief's paper. The memo is the logistics: the general, recording.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d179: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, October 31, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 179. London's Halloween letter. The message is the letter: the prime minister, writing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d279: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 279. The connective joint. The note is the joint: the pieces, meeting.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d379: Bohlen minutes, December 1, 1943 — Document 379. A third. The minutes are the third: the diplomat, tireless.
arxiv-2605-09279: Streaming volumetric video — 3D scenes you can walk around — eats bandwidth. Daheng Yin, Yili Jin, Jianxin Shi, and colleagues adapt to color and content with CAGS: color-adaptive streaming via dynamic 3D Gaussian splatting. The 2026 paper squeezes 3D video through thin pipes.
arxiv-2605-09479: Image quality metrics usually please human eyes; machine consumers — downstream models — want different things. Feng Ding, Haisheng Fu, Jie Liang, and colleagues measure multi-layer CLIP similarity for machine-oriented quality — ML-CLIPSim. The 2026 paper judges images the way AI sees them.
arxiv-2605-09679: Medical vision-language models answering questions about 3D tumor scans need stage-wise evaluation. Yixiong Chen, Wenjie Xiao, Pedro R. A. S. Bassi, and colleagues build DeepTumorVQA: a hierarchical 3D CT benchmark for medical VLMs and tool-augmented agents. The 2026 paper grades medical AI like a residency.
arxiv-2605-09779: Active fluids — swarming bacteria, flocking cells — flip between collective states in rare, dramatic transitions; a weakly nonlinear reduction captures them. Yves-Marie Ducimetière and Michael John Shelley develop the reduction. The 2026 paper is soft-matter physics on rare events.
arxiv-2605-09979: Spin-1 dark matter coupling through the Higgs portal, with parity-violating interactions, could explain the galactic halo's mysterious gamma ray excess. This 2026 paper builds the case carefully. It is particle astrophysics: dark matter with a handedness. It gives the gamma-ray excess a particle explanation.
arxiv-2605-10079: Multi-person video generation with training-free social interaction control — SocialDirector directs the crowd. Liangyang Ouyang, Ruicong Liu, Caixin Kang, and colleagues build it. The 2026 paper is video generation with social choreography. It directs crowded social scenes without any training at all.
plos-pone-0003379: Economists investigated a paradox of free health coverage in this 2008 study of the Philippines. Although the government promoted social health insurance to erase unmet medical needs, poor families were still not using it. Survey evidence revealed barriers to full utilization, showing that offering insurance is not the same as delivering care: access problems must be fixed too.
plos-pone-0003479: Physicists hunted the best wiring for busy networks in this 2008 paper. The shape of a network, its topology, controls how well it transmits information and synchronizes, from brain circuits to power grids. The team developed methods for finding near-optimal layouts in active networks, connecting abstract graph theory to real flowing systems.
plos-pone-0003579: Neuroscientists identified a damage sensor with repair potential in this 2008 paper. GPR17, a newly found receptor resembling purinergic receptors, detects brain injury and sits on the path to making new neurons and myelin-making oligodendrocytes. As a druggable target, it offers a foothold for therapies that would rebuild rather than just protect the injured brain.
plos-pone-0003679: In 2008, Colzato, van den Wildenberg, and Hommel found faith narrowing the mind's eye. Religious belief shifted how people spread visual attention, with believers more likely to miss the big picture for the details. The study shows a cultural force reaching down into the basic mechanics of seeing.
plos-pone-0003779: Petter, Bonow, and Klinkert watched malaria's disguise genes shift during sex-cell making in this 2008 paper. The rif multigene family showed diverse expression patterns as Plasmodium falciparum gametocytes matured. The shifting patterns reveal how the parasite stays hidden while preparing to infect mosquitoes.
plos-pone-0003879: A 2008 immunology study traced asthma's spark to lung sentinels. Pulmonary myeloid dendritic cells grabbed allergens, switched on, and pumped out IL-23, driving the airway overreaction of allergic asthma. The work places these cells at the top of the chain that makes asthmatic lungs twitch.
plos-pone-0003979: In 2008, Druce, Shannon, and Page built an early-warning system for savannas. Their protocol tracks vegetation change to catch ecological thresholds before tipping points. Savanna landscapes can flip states suddenly, so land managers need advance notice. The monitoring framework turns routine field observations into clear actionable alerts for rangers.
plos-pone-0004079: In 2008, a team timed cholesterol's quick inner shiver precisely. Low density lipoproteins reacted fast to small temperature shifts. The nanophase change in LDL's fatty lipid core proved surprisingly quick. The tiny floating particles may double as the blood's own thermometers.
plos-pone-0004179: In 2009, Nagarajan, Parikh, and Garrett-Sinha probed an oncogene in mouse skin. Turning on Ets1 in maturing skin cells caused disorderly growth. The gene switch pushed skin cells toward a precancer state. The mouse model captures early steps of skin tumor growth.
plos-pone-0004279: In 2009, Joppa, Loarie, and Pimm asked if parks help or hurt neighbors. Population growth near protected areas was measured worldwide. The parks' effects on rural communities varied. The study informs conservation planning. The findings guide balancing nature and human needs.
plos-pone-0358979: Göbeklitepe in Türkiye, with its massive stone circles, is among the oldest temple sites on Earth — built before farming began. This paper reports the first burials found there, and what they reveal about Early Neolithic funeral rites. The graves add a human dimension to a site famous for its monuments, showing how its builders honored their dead.
plos-pone-0358879: Thyroid nodules are common and usually harmless — but what predicts them? This cross-sectional study linked the metabolic score for insulin resistance and uric acid levels to prevalent thyroid nodules, factoring in blood pressure. The metabolic connections suggest thyroid screening may belong in metabolic checkups.
plos-pone-0358479: Athletes warm up, wait through halftime, then go cold again. This systematic review with three-level meta-analysis examined re-warm up strategies and their moderators on performance and perceived exertion in team sports. The synthesis tells coaches exactly which half-time routines actually work.
plos-pone-0358179: When Jordanian university students catch a cold, do they reach for herbs or pharmacy drugs? This cross-sectional study mapped their preferences for cold and flu treatment. The preference patterns reveal where traditional herbal medicine still rules campus — and where conventional medicine has won.
plos-pone-0357779: After disasters strike, traffic control must adapt in minutes — not hours. This paper used multi-agent meta-reinforcement learning with contrastive predictive coding for rapid adaptive traffic control after emergencies. The AI system reroutes a stricken city’s traffic with a speed no human dispatcher could match.
plos-pone-0356579: This entry is a retraction notice, not a research finding. The journal has retracted the paper claiming synergistic activity of quercetin with antibiotics against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains. The notice formally removes those findings from the scientific record — a marker of science correcting itself.
plos-pone-0357279: How teachers perceive school-wide teacher-student relations shapes their job satisfaction. This study applied affective events theory to Shanghai teachers, linking perceived relations to satisfaction. The analysis shows that school climate isn’t background noise — it’s central to whether teachers thrive or burn out.
plos-pone-0356879: Hypertensive disorders kill mothers across Nigeria — but targeted programs can turn the tide. This case study described a quality improvement program addressing risk factors for hypertensive disorders in pregnancy across two Nigerian states. The program’s results offer a replicable model for saving mothers’ lives.
plos-pone-0355379: The COVID-19 pandemic shook religious faith to its foundations in Poland. This study examined theodicy perspectives — how believers reconcile a good God with terrible suffering — as an effect of interpenetrating mental and religious struggles during the pandemic. The findings map faith under extreme pressure.
plos-pone-0356779: Genes for longevity may also tune how fiercely the immune system responds to infection. This dairy goat study tested the effect of longevity genotype on the acute phase response to a lipopolysaccharide challenge. The genetics reveal a fascinating trade-off between long life and immune vigor.
plos-pone-0356479: Zambia’s Farm Block Development Program promises rural transformation — but what do residents think? This paper captured community perspectives and evaluated household income factors in Kawambwa district. The ground-level lessons should temper — and improve — top-down agricultural policy.
plos-pone-0357179: In glaucoma AI, how you label the training data changes everything. This multicenter machine learning study showed labeling choices materially affect visual field progression prediction. The finding is a cautionary tale: labels aren’t neutral, and modelers ignore that at patients’ peril.
plos-pone-0346479: Wireless sensor networks die when their batteries do — smart routing extends their lives. EZS-SEP is a hybrid efficient zonal stable election routing protocol with SOM-based node deployment for heterogeneous networks. The protocol squeezes far more operational life from scattered sensors.
plos-pone-0356179: Internationally educated nurses are healthcare’s lifeline — but integrating and retaining them is hard. This paper took an ecosystem perspective on building sustainable talent pipelines for these nurses. The systems view reveals the interlocking supports that turn foreign-trained nurses into rooted, thriving professionals.
plos-pone-0355479: Cities follow mathematical scaling laws — and they did millennia ago too. This paper traced the emergence of urban scaling in Ancient Southwest Asia. Finding modern scaling patterns in Bronze Age cities suggests deep, universal principles govern how human settlements organize — from Uruk to New York.
plos-pone-0354179: MOFU — a MOrphing Fluffy Unit — is a soft robot that expands and contracts like a breathing creature. This paper described its development and evaluated the animacy of its movements. The research probes what makes motion feel alive — insights that could make future companion robots genuinely comforting rather than merely mechanical.
plos-pone-0355179: Quantum computers will break today’s encryption — so post-quantum cryptography must run on tiny embedded chips. This paper explored the hardware implementation feasibility of NIST-standardized ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA on embedded systems. The evaluation shows which quantum-safe algorithms can realistically protect the Internet of Things.
plos-pone-0356279: Measuring how people cope with stress shouldn’t require an exhausting questionnaire. This paper tested the psychometric properties of a short form of the Coping Inventory for Stressful Situations — the CISS-SF. The validated short form gives researchers and clinicians a quick, trustworthy window into coping styles.
plos-pone-0356079: Measuring genetic diversity sounds simple — until you need statistical rigor. This paper evaluated genetic diversity differences within a likelihood framework. The principled statistical approach gives population geneticists trustworthy tools for comparing diversity across groups — the foundation of conservation genetics.
plos-pone-0354079: Nursing home residents kept getting COVID-19 despite strong vaccine responses — a disturbing paradox. This paper documented high SARS-CoV-2 reinfection rates in long-term care residents despite robust spike-specific immunity after serial vaccination. The findings reveal that antibodies alone don’t protect the frail elderly — reshaping how we think about protecting care homes.
plos-pone-0335879: High school students in Lomé, Togo navigate sexual risks with limited guidance. This cross-sectional study measured risky sexual behaviors and their associated factors. The findings give Togolese health educators the local evidence to design interventions that speak to teenagers’ actual lives rather than adult assumptions.
plos-pone-0355679: Climate-smart farming promises resilience — but Ghana’s smallholders aren’t adopting it. This paper examined the challenges to adoption among smallholder farmers in semi-arid Ghana. The findings reveal the economic, informational, and cultural barriers standing between good agronomy and the farmers who need it most.
plos-pone-0355279: Cloud storage needs encryption that lets authorized parties re-encrypt data without seeing it. This paper proposed an efficient lattice-based identity-based proxy re-encryption scheme with direct revocation. The quantum-resistant cryptography prepares cloud security for the post-quantum era.
plos-pone-0354879: Men with acute urinary retention face a timing question: remove the catheter early or late? This Dutch national randomized trial protocol will test early versus delayed trial without catheter. The planned trial brings rigorous evidence to a daily urological dilemma affecting thousands.
plos-pone-0354679: Low serotonin may prime the trigeminal system for migraine. This rat study showed serotonin depletion amplifies migraine susceptibility through trigeminal ganglion neuron sensitization, with patch clamp evidence. The findings mechanistically link the classic serotonin hypothesis to the neurons where migraine pain begins.
plos-pone-0353179: Mental health projects for veterans and first responders — do they pay off? This paper estimated the return on investment of such wellbeing projects. The economic valuation gives funders hard numbers for programs whose value is usually described only in stories.
europmc-pmc2832679: Some gene-silencing proteins can shut down DNA from a distance. This 2010 paper shows KRAB-zinc finger proteins and KAP1 mediate long-range transcriptional repression through the spreading of heterochromatin, tightly packed DNA. The authors map how the silencing travels. The mechanism explains how cells keep large genome regions switched off.
europmc-pmc2867979: Medical journals favor happy results, warping what doctors believe. This 2010 narrative review surveys reporting bias in medical research. The authors gather how bias creeps in, from hidden trials to spun abstracts, and what it costs patients. Their review armed readers with healthy skepticism about the published record.
europmc-pmc2874579: Dry eye burns millions, and tears carry clues. This 2010 paper analyzes immune signals in tears from evaporative dry eye disease and ties them to symptoms. The authors' tear profiles reveal the inflammation within the eye. Their work points toward targeted drops that calm the right signals.
europmc-pmc2916879: Flu viruses adapt to new hosts with tiny tweaks. This 2010 paper characterizes a host-adapting amino acid in influenza virus, biologically and structurally. The authors pin down the exact change that helps the jump between species. Their work illuminates what makes a pandemic strain.
europmc-pmc2922379: Fatty food, gut germs, and inflammation form a vicious chain. This 2010 mouse study shows high-fat diet and bacteria interactions promote intestinal inflammation that precedes obesity and insulin resistance. The authors catch the sequence. Their work put gut bugs at the start of metabolic disease.
europmc-pmc2949879: Modeling brain electricity needs open tools anyone can use. This 2010 paper introduces OpenMEEG, open-source software for quasistatic bioelectromagnetics. The authors' toolkit models EEG and MEG signals. Their software spread through neuroscience labs. Researchers model head currents with it daily.
europmc-pmc2984379: Diabetes will surge by 2050, this 2010 model warns. The authors project US adult diabetes cases with a dynamic model of new cases and deaths. Their forecast alarmed policymakers. The work shaped prevention planning. One in three adults may carry it by then.
europmc-pmc3025879: Hearts got 4D blood flow movies. This 2011 review covers full 4D flow mapping of the heart and great vessels by MRI. The authors survey the technique's power. Their overview guides heart doctors. Surgeons preview repairs in the flow field. Valve repairs get rehearsed in the flow.
europmc-pmc3042979: The brain throbs with each heartbeat. This 2011 review surveys studies of the brain's pulse inside the skull. The authors link strong pulses to disease. Their work informs brain surgery. Stiff brains pulse harder, they find. Surgeons watch the pulse during operations.
europmc-pmc3046479: DNA libraries got fast and cheap. This 2010 paper brings a quick recipe for sequencing libraries from tiny DNA inputs. The authors' trick cut costs sharply. It spread through genomics labs. Single cells became sequenceable overnight. The method is now sold in kits.
europmc-pmc3048379: Motor learning bends with mental strategy. This 2011 paper shows thinkers switch tactics while learning new movements. The authors reveal the mind's steering role. Their work informs rehab. Explicit plans speed early learning most. Stroke rehab now coaches strategy, not just reps.
europmc-pmc6526279: Alzheimer's begins silently, with subtle slips in memory, movement, and behavior years before diagnosis. This paper argues that phones and wearables can catch those early whispers: typing patterns, gait, sleep, and speech collected passively become digital biomarkers. Continuous, at-home monitoring could flag decline far earlier than clinic visits - and measure whether treatments work.
europmc-pmc6537279: Long before COVID-19, coronaviruses like SARS and MERS showed the family's pandemic potential. This 2019 review focuses on the envelope protein - a small but essential component that helps the virus assemble and provoke inflammation. Understanding this protein's roles offered clues for vaccines and drugs against current and future coronavirus threats.
europmc-pmc6557979: Mesenchymal stem cells are prized for calming runaway immune responses in sepsis, transplants, and autoimmune disease - yet how they do it stayed murky. This review compares living, dying, and dead MSCs, finding that even apoptotic and dead cells can soothe immunity through the signals they release. The insight reframes what makes cell therapy work.
europmc-pmc6558879: Alpha-synuclein is famous as the Parkinson's protein - but it also meddles in Alzheimer's. This review gathers evidence that the presynaptic protein accumulates in Alzheimer's brains alongside amyloid and tau, potentially worsening damage. The overlap suggests the two diseases share more machinery than thought, with synuclein as a possible joint target.
europmc-pmc6571179: Heart-attack blood tests may double as crystal balls: tiny amounts of troponin T and I leak from stressed hearts even in healthy people. This study measured both in the general population to see whether they predict future heart disease equally. The comparison helps doctors decide if these markers belong in routine risk screening.
europmc-pmc6602479: Behind countless papers sits the EMBL-EBI's free toolkit: sequence search, alignment, and analysis apps plus a powerful text search across biological databases. This 2019 update describes the programmatic APIs that let researchers pipe these services into their own pipelines. The interfaces keep Europe's bioinformatics engine room open to all.
europmc-pmc6716579: Babies are seeded with microbes at birth - but which microbes come from where? Tracking mothers and infants, this study mapped microbial transmission from the mother's gut, vagina, skin, and mouth to the newborn's gut. The route map shows the maternal reservoir shaping the infant's first ecosystem.
europmc-pmc6723779: Gum disease is an ecosystem gone rogue - plaque biofilms provoke the immune system into destroying the tooth's foundations. This review unpacks periodontitis: how bacterial communities and inflammation conspire to dissolve gum and bone. The multifaceted disease demands more than brushing alone.
europmc-pmc6738079: Starved of oxygen and nutrients, cancer cells rewire their fat metabolism to survive. This review examines how tumors balance making their own fatty acids against stealing them from outside under metabolic stress. The lipid juggling act exposes vulnerabilities drug designers can exploit.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-79: A 2007 Government Accountability Office report warning that the Census Bureau needed to improve its risk management of the computer systems built for the decennial count. With 2010 approaching, the systems for collecting and processing census data faced schedule and performance risks. GAO's findings preview the IT troubles that would later force the bureau to scrap and rebuild parts of its 2010 technology.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-879: Mobile-home buyers deserved a fair shake in 2007 — GAO's report says the housing agency should study how proposed loan-rule changes would hit them. The findings put the spotlight on factory-built housing, the most affordable roof for millions. Policy tweaks, GAO warns, land hardest on those with the thinnest margins.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-679: Counting the true cost of government was a coin toss in 2007 — GAO's report finds cost-accounting habits varied wildly across ten agencies. The findings show a Tower of Babel in budget-speak. The report's plea: one honest math, so managers can actually manage.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-379: The Doha trade talks were at a crossroads in 2007, and GAO's report says Congress faced key decisions as the push intensified. The findings frame the choices. The report warns that the round the world was watching could collapse on America's watch.
openalex-w7206151279: Who we are, our feelings, ideas, and sense of reality, is shaped by the people and media around us, and the internet is now central to that. This paper examines how online life produces subjectivity and what that means for learning. It argues that understanding how students see themselves and the world is part of understanding how they learn. More philosophy of education than lab study, it connects digital culture to the classroom.
openalex-w7205014679: Learning to read should feel like play, not drill. This article studies how playful, game-like strategies help young children take their first steps into literacy. The authors review approaches for the early school years and what makes them work. Warm and practical, it argues that joy is not the opposite of rigor in teaching reading; it is the engine.
openalex-w7204643479: Real inclusion means more than a seat in the classroom. This article argues that teacher training and new teaching habits are what move inclusive education from paper promises to genuine learning. The authors study how preparing teachers differently changes what happens for students with disabilities. A qualitative study with a clear message: inclusion is built by teachers, one lesson at a time.
openalex-w7129018379: Physical literacy, the motivation and skill to stay active for life, is gaining global attention. This narrative review surveys the concept's status in Japan: research, practice, and the missing national definition. The authors noted the sports agency's 2022 move. A policy-flavored review of getting a nation moving.
openalex-w7140293179: Children who beat leukemia may fear its return for years. This paper studied fear of cancer recurrence and how it affects taking medicines among young survivors in low-resource settings. The authors linked anxiety to adherence. A pediatric-oncology study of the worry that outlives the cure.
openalex-w7148264079: Heart failure keeps sending patients back to the hospital. This paper proposes a bold fix: planned admissions before patients visibly worsen. The authors argued that poor self-management drives readmissions. A cardiology strategy paper betting that scheduled care beats crisis care.
pmc-13492279: A 2026 drug-discovery paper combining chemoinformatics with machine learning to find an existing drug that might fight a neglected disease. The pipeline flagged chlormidazole as a repurposing candidate — a drug approved for one use that may work against another. Repurposing is valuable because it can cut years and costs off the road to treatment.
pmc-13464279: A 2026 cardiology case report with a twist: a recurrent cardiac tumor that looked like a myxoma — the most common benign heart tumor — turned out to be something else. "When Recurrent Myxoma Is Not a Myxoma" walks through the diagnostic detective work. Cases like this remind clinicians that recurrence should prompt a second look.
pmc-13438179: This 2026 paper contributes further data to the Alzheimer's coverage-with-evidence-development debate — the question of when insurers should pay for new Alzheimer's drugs while more evidence is gathered. The authors add evidence to inform the policy. It sits at the intersection of medicine, economics, and access.
pmc-13475379: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of anti-HER2 therapies in metastatic colorectal cancer. HER2 drugs transformed breast cancer care; the pooled evidence tests their value in colon cancer. The review guides oncologists on when to reach for them.
pmc-13280779: This 2026 veterinary paper covered clinical management of Helicobacter infection in captive baboons, plus isolation and molecular characterization of the bacteria. Primate colonies need tailored infection control. The molecular characterization is the scientific contribution.
pmc-13620179: A 2026 Korean nationwide retrospective cohort study of cardiovascular disease incidence and lipid-lowering medication use in adults with dyslipidemia. Population-scale data reveal treatment gaps. The findings inform national prevention.
pmc-13465679: A 2026 food science paper optimizing formulation parameters for reduced-fat katima — a traditional pastry — using response surface methodology. Healthier traditional foods need careful reformulation. The optimization is the method.
pmc-13453479: A 2026 battery paper on engineering bilayer SEI — the solid-electrolyte interphase — via ultrasonic fields for long-life lithium batteries. Sound waves structured the protective layer. The ultrasonic method is the innovation.
pmc-13423479: A 2026 review on the design and application of nanozymes — current trends and cutting-edge breakthroughs. Nanomaterials that act like enzymes are a hot field. The review surveys it.
pmc-13602379: In this 2026 aquaculture paper, different rainbow trout genetic lines showed varying susceptibility to infectious disease. Genetics shape fish immunity. The line comparison guides breeding.
pmc-13593579: This 2026 paper introduced OpenEvidence — the title suggests an open evidence platform, though the record gives no abstract. The entry is preserved as published. Thin evidence limits what can be said.
pmc-13560079: This 2026 Stockholm study associated infrarenal aortic diameter in siblings within the abdominal aortic aneurysm screening program. Family patterns informed screening. The sibling data are the contribution.
pmc-13448279: This 2026 conference abstract (DSAI-09) presented an interpretable radiomics risk signature distinguishing tumor recurrence from radiation necrosis in brain metastases on post-treatment MRI. Telling regrowth from radiation damage is critical. The signature is the tool.
pmc-13516679: A 2026 veterinary paper on oxidative stress and inflammatory responses in horses naturally infected with Theileria equi. The tick-borne parasite's systemic effects were measured. The responses characterize the disease.
pmc-13512979: A 2026 cardiology paper on HLM staging and SGLT2 inhibitor treatment benefit across heart failure severity. The diabetes drugs' heart benefits were staged. The staging analysis guides use.
pmc-13478879: This 2026 review covered nickel-based anode materials in potassium-ion batteries — review and perspectives. The next-generation batteries need better anodes. The review surveys the candidates.
pmc-13469679: A 2026 paper on a hardware-software integrated PCB image registration method based on local adaptive KNN and SIFT. The circuit board inspection was automated. The registration is the tool.
pmc-13429279: In this 2026 DRC study, factors associated with cervical cancer awareness among women of reproductive age were examined — evidence from a nationwide survey (the title is truncated). The awareness gaps were identified. The factors guide campaigns.
pmc-13524079: This 2026 plant paper showed the primary nitrate response transcription factors TGA1 and TGA4 are negative regulators of sulfate uptake and metabolism. The nitrogen-sulfur crosstalk was mapped. The negative regulation is the mechanism.
pmc-13526479: A 2026 clinicopathologic diagnosis of eosinophilic cellulitis (Wells syndrome) in an elderly patient. The rare skin disease was characterized. The diagnosis is the lesson.
pmc-13467679: A 2026 chemistry paper on sequence-controlled synthesis of heteroaryl-substituted decahydroacridine-1,8-diones — comparative evaluation of preformed enaminone and multicomponent routes (the title is truncated). The synthesis routes were compared. The evaluation is the methodology.
pmc-13467779: A 2026 paper with comparative experimental Raman, DFT, and chemometric characterization of selected phenolic acids — structural and environmental contributions to the vibrational spectra (the title is truncated). The acids' spectra were decoded. The characterization is the analytical resource.
pmc-13452379: A 2026 thyroid cancer paper with comparative assessment of serum adipokine and trace element alterations in papillary thyroid carcinoma. The metabolic markers were compared. The alterations are the finding.
